Segments 14-24 stay small in the batch-size estimate, but from segment 25 onward the step sizes jump noticeably, pushing the estimated batch size up to around 226 — that looks like where the device switch happens. I want to trace how it continues growing in the segments after that.

Checking the math against the claimed total cost of 4.58: the early flat segments account for roughly 1.25, so the post-switch segments would need to average much higher to make up the rest — but my earlier single-point probes at segments 30 and 39 didn't show that kind of blowup. That makes me suspect each profiling call spins up its own fresh replica with an independently randomized switch point, so isolated probes aren't reliable for tracking the ramp — I should trust the contiguous pre-switch measurements instead, which look fairly flat.

Given the switch occurs somewhere in the 16-32 range and post-switch behavior jumps and grows, getting a controller that closes a 9% gap to the 4.18 reference will be nontrivial. I'm planning to run a contiguous profile across segments 24-39 alternating between two batch sizes (like 256 and 2048) to separate out how the scale parameter and the base cost evolve after the switch, budgeting the cost carefully against my remaining evaluation allowance.
